what: Files::relative (cx.rs:64) with root "" strips the leading / of an absolute path: root.trim_end_matches("/") is "", path.strip_prefix("") always matches, then strip_prefix("/") turns "/var/x/probe.rs" into "var/x/probe.rs". Its doc says a root of "" keeps each path whole. Fix: `if root.is_empty() { return path; }` after the trim (a root of "/" trims to "" too: names stay absolute, as rustc run at / would still print a path given absolute... rustc prints the path as given, so keeping it whole is right for both). Breaks blaze-engine as_rustc::tests::anyhow_backtrace_probe (round6-test.log): probe.rs calls Files::new(&paths, "") with the probe named by its absolute path (as rustc names a file given on the command line), the diag names `var/...`, emit::Sources finds no such file and emit.rs:345 panics `a file that can't be read`.
